title: approval-escrow-for-progressive-model-promotions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement an approval-escrow system for progressive model promotions (canary, A/B, shadow) that combines RBAC, timeboxed sign-offs, cryptographic evidence bundles, and automated rollback triggers. Goal is to provide a guardrail-free path for teams to run low-friction progressive rollouts while preserving auditability and rapid remediation for regressions.

Background & motivation:
- Observability and rollout tooling continue to improve, but we lack a standard, auditable flow that enforces required approvals, time-limited entitlements, and machine-verifiable sign-off artifacts for production model promotions.
- Current ad-hoc signoffs (Slack + PR checks) are brittle for Dedicated/Private customers who require clear forensic artifacts and fine-grain RBAC mapping.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Approval Escrow: a short-lived signed approval object stored with the rollout config. Approvals include approver identity, scope (model id, route, percentage), validity window, and a signature (KMS/HSM). The control plane only honors rollouts that reference a valid escrow.
2) Entitlement Roles: Define role templates (Reviewer, Owner, Compliance, Platform) mapped to IAM principals and group IDs. Roles express minimum approvers and quorum rules.
3) Policy-as-code Gates: Integrate with OPA/Rego to evaluate automated checks (SLO regressions, testset failure thresholds, sensitive prompt detection) before allowing an approval to be issued into escrow.
4) Timeboxed Sign-offs & Escalation: Sign-offs expire automatically at end of window; if escalation required, a secondary approver group is notified and a remediations window starts.
5) Audit Evidence Bundle: On approval, attach links to artifacts (PR, eval run id, dashboard snapshot) and hash them into the escrow. Store the bundle in immutable audit store and expose UI download for forensic teams.
6) Auto-rollback hooks: If runtime monitors detect drift or customer reported incidents that match a severity threshold, the control plane enacts rollback using the rollback-escrow and notifies owners. Rollbacks are also recorded as evidence.

Acceptance criteria:
- Console UI: flow to create, review, sign, and revoke approval escrows for a rollout (canary/AB/shadow).
- API: endpoints to create approval escrows, validate signatures, and query audit bundles.
- RBAC: mapping UI that ties roles to Org groups and service principals; must support grant-by-service-account for automated CI approvals.
- Evidence: audit bundle schema, storage path, and download link for each approval; hashed and signed.
- Policy integration: OPA policy endpoint stub and at least 3 example policies (SLO check, eval-failure threshold, PII-detection block).
- Auto-rollback: rule engine hooks and a simulated test where a metric regression triggers rollback and generates audit artifacts.

Non-goals:
- Not building a full SIEM pipeline (we will export logs to existing Splunk/Datadog integration).
- Not replacing org-level IAM providers; we will integrate via SCIM/group sync and service account mapping.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Adding cryptographic signing adds complexity (KMS costs, HSM access for some customers).
- Timeboxed approvals could create friction for small on-call teams; we must provide sensible defaults and escalation paths.
- Storing evidence bundles increases DB/storage usage; use object storage with lifecycle rules.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (MVP, 3 sprints):
- Approval escrow spec and JSON schema (design doc).
- API endpoints: create/validate/list escrows; KMS sign/verify integration.
- Simple Console modal for request/review/approve with evidence links.
- Basic RBAC mapping (org groups -> roles).
- Demo: internal canary promotion using approval escrow.

Phase 2 (policy & auto-rollback):
- OPA integration and example policies.
- Auto-rollback rules engine and simulator.
- Audit export hooks to Splunk and export retention policy.

Phase 3 (enterprise features):
- Multi-approver quorum, delegated approvals expiration, and delegated escrow transfer.
- HSM-backed signing for private deployments; stronger compliance reports.

Open questions:
- Should automated CI approvals (unit/regression evals) be allowed to sign escrows without human intervention? (proposed: yes if signed by service-account with explicit grant and tied to eval id)
- Default expiry window length for escrows (proposal: 72 hours).
- Minimum quorum for enterprise tenants (configurable).
